claims.text: Rapidly solidified equiatomic FeCoNi is a single-phase FCC high-entropy alloy.
Rapidly solidified equiatomic FeCoNi exhibits soft ferromagnetism with a low coercive field.
Annealing rapidly solidified FeCoNi at 400–600°C can nucleate coherent nanoscale precipitates or induce short-range chemical ordering.
The annealing treatment can produce nanoscale features while preserving a single FCC phase.
The relevant structural mediator is a population of coherent nanoscale precipitates or chemically ordered regions within the FCC matrix.
The annealing-induced nanoscale features act as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
The annealing-induced nanoscale features enhance local magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Domain-wall pinning and enhanced local magnetocrystalline anisotropy increase coercivity.
Annealed FeCoNi will have greater coercivity than untreated FeCoNi.
Annealed FeCoNi will have greater coercivity than FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt derivatives.
The coercivity increase may be approximately 50% or more.
The annealed alloy will maintain other desirable magnetic properties.
FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt satisfy the stated high-entropy-alloy compositional and entropy criteria.
FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt exhibit soft ferromagnetism with low coercivity.
Annealing conditions influence phase stability and the length scale of decomposition or ordering.
Careful selection of annealing temperature and duration can avoid phase separation or detrimental secondary phases in FeCoNi.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires retention of a single FCC phase and treats phase transformation as falsifying, yet one proposed mediator is precipitation, which ordinarily implies formation of a compositionally or structurally distinct phase. Short-range ordering could remain single-phase, but the precipitate branch is not reconciled with the single-phase requirement.
